issues.description: The culpable-auditor program names the AAER response CSV and three manually prepared Excel workbooks. None is in the assigned package; their author-specific fields, versions, and rights need confirmation.

The Stata source splits an existing full part_a into part_a_1/part_a_2 and later merges User records using part_a.dta by user_id_new. The exact producer and version of the full part_a dataset remain unresolved.

The SAS source has three separate User import blocks, outputs them as a.partc_1/a.partc_2/a.partc_3, appends them, and matches by state/title. The supplied Stata evidence shows part_a_1/part_a_2 and m_/i_ position intermediates; their producer relation and exact schema remain unresolved.

SAS imports six education*_matched tables and consumes bachelor_date, while the local raw Revelio Education product has different fields. The code does not establish the matched-file producer, match inputs, or bachelor_date derivation.

The source labels a Compustat fuzzy-match step and SAS consumes funda_matched.dta, but the exact match producer, score rules, and manual verification records are unresolved; screened code blocks are not used to infer them.

The active SAS path joins b.remaining, b.remaining_final, and b.goodluck; the shown manual import/recoding blocks are commented, leaving the classifications as author-prepared inputs with no supplied producer artifact.

The supplied SAS comments say paper labor-market tables use old b.partb_final instead of the newly created a.partb_final, and the active analysis reads b.partb_final. The historical snapshot and intended refresh rule are unresolved.

The Stata/SAS code is embedded in a PDF and uses distinct file/library handoffs. Extract/reflow and coherent batch-root configuration are needed before any separately authorized run; no path literal is reproduced in the corrected excerpts.

The appendix and datasheet describe manual real-estate transaction collection and a 200-person comparison sample, but the supplied code ends after sorting the sample and does not include transaction-analysis code or a produced transaction file.
SAS availability/version and DBMS=STATA import support were not verified under the authorized checks; no SAS executable or startup was invoked.

evidence.description: The authors manually review SEC/PCAOB orders to identify audit-related culpable auditors.
evidence.quote:
1) We first download all enforcement orders directly from the SEC and PCAOB website.
          We then read each enforcement order to identify instances in which a respondent
          named in the enforcement action was employed by an accounting firm at the time of
          the alleged misconduct, and the enforcement was against audit related misconduct.

evidence.description: Manual enforcement collection includes date, violation year, auditor name, age, title, employer, and penalty.
evidence.quote:
unique observation. We collect details including the enforcement date, the violation
       year, the nature of the violation, and for each culpable auditor: name, age, job title,
       employer, and the penalty imposed by the regulator.

evidence.description: LexisNexis searches use auditor identity and employment details to identify property records.
evidence.quote:
4) To obtain personal outcomes for culpable auditor sample in step (1), we use the
       culpable individual’s name, age, state where the culpable auditor is located (all
       obtained directly from the enforcement orders) as searching parameters in LexisNexis.
       We use individual’s CPA license number, employer, and job title to narrow down the

evidence.description: The authors manually collect property purchase/sale details and cash flows around a three-year window.
evidence.quote:
search results and identify the right person. We then review the culpable auditors’
       real estate ownership holdings and identify buying and selling transactions for the
       three-year window before and after the misconduct enforcement order release date.
       We collect the details about cash flow effects of these purchases (repurchases) and
       sales.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes Position Files fields and an IPA100 employer screen.
evidence.quote:
1) We first download all Position Files from Revelio which contain information on
       individuals’ employer name, region, country, state, employment start date,
       employment end date, and title.
    2) We then merge all Position Files by limiting individuals that work in United States
       using the ‘country’ field.
    3) We then fuzzy match and only keep those that ever work at the top 100 largest
       professional service firms from Inside Public Accounting (IPA 100).

actions.description: Obtain the author-specific Audit Analytics AAER respondent CSV or an author-approved licensed route and data dictionary.
steps: Confirm the product, licensed delivery route, extraction date/version, and fields date, aaerreleaseno, and aaereventkey.
Keep the authors' 2003–2019 sample restriction and do not substitute an unverified public feed.
validation: After an authorized file is obtained, compare its field names, date coverage, and row-level event keys to the source contract without running the author program.

actions.description: Resolve the author-prepared workbook, partner-master, manual classification, and prior-snapshot contracts as a single versioned input set.
steps: Request the exact SEC.KLMP.xlsx, PCAOB.KLMP.xlsx, KLMP.xlsx, match partner list.dta, b.remaining/b.remaining_final, b.goodluck, and b.partb_final artifacts with their original dates and data dictionaries.
Clarify the producer and manual-review rules for each crosswalk, whether old b.partb_final must be used for paper tables, and the intended refresh/version rule.
Preserve filenames, workbook sheets, license restrictions, and hashes; do not reconstruct the manual classifications from public sources without an authorized specification.
validation: When authorized artifacts are supplied, confirm sheet/table names and the consumed fields in the routes, then check join-key uniqueness and version consistency before any author execution.

actions.description: Resolve the exact Revelio product bundle, as-of dates, and author-side field mapping for the Position, User, and Education stages.
steps: Ask for the exact author CSV bundle and product vintage that supplies company_name, title_raw, first/last name, and the matched bachelor_date output.
Clarify conversions from the local SAS product fields, including rcid/company-name mapping, name derivation, Education-to-bachelor_date logic, and the output split/match procedure.
Keep local catalog candidates as unresolved alternatives until every consumed field, coverage period, and producer role is documented.
validation: For any approved local or vendor route, compare the full product schema and snapshot dates to the exact author fields and check representative historical coverage without executing the Stata/SAS program.

actions.description: Resolve the full part_a input and the distinct three-file User handoff before defining a Stata-to-SAS run order.
steps: Ask the authors to identify the producer and version of part_a.dta and document how user1.dta/user2.dta/user3.dta are created.
Map each generated filename to its exact Stata or SAS consumer and supply the original column definitions, partition boundaries, and file locations.
Keep the existing part_a_1/part_a_2 handoff distinct from the user1/user2/user3 inputs until the authors confirm their relationship.
validation: After the producer contract is supplied, verify each named output exists in the authorized working tree and carries the consumer's required keys/fields before running any author program.

actions.description: Acquire the historical IPA100 input matching the authors' 2024 ipa_070424.dta file or obtain its exact author-approved route.
steps: Confirm the exact 2024 list, firm_1 field preparation, and any title/company normalization from the authors.
Treat the public IPA page as a candidate route only; its current Excel offering does not establish the 2024 input file.
validation: Check the acquired list's vintage, firm-name coverage, and firm_1 mapping before using it in any authorized program run.

actions.description: Resolve the licensed Compustat inputs, fuzzy-match handoff, manual checks, and the author market_cap construction.
steps: Request the exact Compustat COMPANY/FUNDA vintages, the author-generated funda_matched.dta and b.klmp products, and any manual match adjudication file.
Confirm the mapping from COMP.COMPANY.conm to the author name-match fields and from local FUNDA mkvalt/prcc_f/csho fields to author market_cap, gvkeyn, fyear, and tic.
Clarify match score thresholds and enforcement-year joins; do not infer or substitute a market-cap definition.
validation: Before any execution, verify the full schema, vintage, unique gvkey-year coverage, the author mapping, and matched-file producer/consumer consistency.

actions.description: Obtain the exact six education matched-file producers and bachelor_date definition used by the real-estate comparison.
steps: Request the producer, matching keys, degree filters, date interpretation, and output schema for education1_1 through education3_2 matched files.
Resolve whether the local raw Education candidate is the author's source and how startdate/enddate/degree are transformed to bachelor_date.
validation: Confirm all six named inputs, bachelor_date definition, and user_id coverage against the comparison sample before any author run.

actions.description: Resolve the licensed manual real-estate records and the omitted transaction-analysis stage needed for the documented companion analysis.
steps: Ask for any author-held transaction/address-history tables, their data dictionary, selection keys, collection period, and permissible access route.

Clarify whether a separate transaction-analysis script or results file exists beyond the supplied final sort, and whether the 200-person comparison sample is the intended full extent of the code package.

actions.description: Prepare a working copy of the embedded Stata/SAS code and replace author-machine paths with coherent batch-mode roots before a separately authorized run.
steps: Extract/reflow the PDF code into versioned working-copy files while preserving the original PDF and documenting the source line mapping.
Choose one working directory and consistent relative paths for each Stata/SAS producer-consumer handoff; keep absolute Dropbox paths out of executable configuration.
Preserve the original program design, samples, variable definitions, and manual inputs while resolving paths.
validation: Review the proposed file map against every active import/export and library reference; verify each path resolves inside the approved working tree before any authorized execution.

actions.description: Confirm an authorized batch SAS environment and its Stata DTA import/export support using deployment documentation when available.
steps: Confirm SAS version, batch invocation, required DBMS=STATA engine, and the approved work-directory setup through documented host configuration.
Use no interactive startup, executable, version, or autoexec check in this feasibility assessment.
validation: After the host setup is confirmed, verify only the documented SAS/DBMS capability and path configuration before a separately authorized author-code run.

actions.description: Conditional native run sequence for the embedded Stata and SAS workflow, preserving the observed Stata-to-SAS, Stata Step 8, and return-to-SAS handoffs and pausing at the documented missing input and producer contracts.
steps: Before any separately authorized run, reflow the PDF-embedded Stata and SAS sections into versioned working copies, map source lines, and configure coherent batch working roots and libraries. Confirm the SAS runtime and DBMS=STATA import setup; preserve the source statements and do not execute while required contracts remain unresolved.

Culpable-auditor Stata block: first resolve the AAER response extract, the SEC and PCAOB workbooks, the KLMP Final manual sheet, their dates, fields, and rights. Then run the supplied block in its source order through its eststo logit models and esttab output. Stop before this block if any required author-prepared input contract is absent.

Comparison-auditor Stata preparation: import and filter the Revelio Position inputs as supplied, preserve the user/employer/state/date/title fields, run the position-matching stage, and construct its m_/i_ intermediates and departing-user history outputs. Keep these products distinct from the full part_a master and the later SAS User split inputs.

At the full part_a gate, obtain the producer, version, schema, and working-tree location for part_a.dta. The source shows part_a_1.dta and part_a_2.dta being split from an existing full part_a and a later User merge using part_a.dta by user_id_new; do not infer the full producer from those consumers. Pause until that contract is supplied.

Once part_a.dta is confirmed, continue the supplied Stata sequence: create the two part_a partitions, then carry out the later User merge by user_id_new. Hand part_a_1.dta and part_a_2.dta to SAS as the code specifies; do not map them to the separate three-file User input branch without author confirmation.

Part 2 comparison-auditor SAS stage: after SAS batch/runtime and library setup, import both Stata partitions with DBMS=STATA and append them into a.part_a. Continue in source order using the author partner master and its documented state/title matching fields, the specified t-2 through t+1 turnover window, and the top-100 list joined by firm_1. Pause at any missing author master, list, runtime, or field contract.

At the SAS-to-Stata Step 8 handoff, form the documented a.test subset with company_name1, row_num, and enforcement_year for Compustat name matching. The source labels a Stata fuzzy-match stage and SAS later consumes funda_matched.dta, but the active producer, match thresholds, manual decisions, and output contract are unresolved. Do not run or infer that stage until those exact details are supplied.

After the Step 8 producer and output are confirmed, return to SAS: import funda_matched.dta, join the matched names by company_name1, then join the Compustat firm-year data by gvkey and enforcement year/fyear. Resolve the author market_cap construction and all consumed company/fundamentals fields before proceeding; do not substitute a definition or infer a match score.

Continue the SAS branch with the author-prepared b.remaining, b.remaining_final, and b.goodluck inputs consumed by active joins. The shown workbook-import blocks are commented; keep them inactive and obtain their separate producer/schema contracts. Confirm the old b.partb_final snapshot and intended refresh rule because the paper-table path reads it instead of the newly made a.partb_final.

For the later User and education branch, resolve the producer and schema for each of the three distinct SAS User imports before appending and matching by state/title. Preserve that branch separately from part_a_1/part_a_2. Then follow the supplied real-estate section: form its unique user_id key set, stack the six matched education tables, and join bachelor_date by user_id.

The supplied real-estate code proceeds to select the 200-person comparison controls and ends at a sort. Stop at that code endpoint unless the authors supply the transaction records and the omitted transaction-analysis stage, including its producer, keys, date window, and consumed fields; do not claim the companion transaction analysis is supplied or executed.
validation: Before each authorized native stage, verify its exact source files, workbook sheets/tables, runtime, and all consumed fields/keys; stop at unresolved producer and version gates instead of inferring filenames or substituting another branch.

After a separately authorized stage, check the documented handoffs and key continuity for part_a_1/part_a_2 to a.part_a, the SAS no-match subset to the Step 8 result and back to SAS, and the distinct User/education branch without changing the source analysis.

Treat the final 200-person control selection and sort as the endpoint of the supplied real-estate code. Transaction analysis requires the missing transaction source and analysis-stage contract; this procedure asserts no execution outcome.
